This record is the South Carolina chapter by G. E. Siple (printed p. 212-217 = PDF pages 218-223) of the whole Water-Supply Paper 1222. Only PDF pages 218-223 were used; pages 199-217 (Maryland, North Carolina) and 224-229 (Tennessee) in this packet belong to other chapters and were not recorded. 17 observation wells: each gets the highest (groundwater head) and lowest (observation water_level) water level of record as stated in the text; the 1952 measurement tables were not transcribed. Numbers are written without the OCR spaces (e.g. '94. 50' -> 94.50); 'Isd' is OCR for lsd (land-surface datum). Figure 31 (well map) and Figure 32 (Sumter well 1 hydrograph) not read. 1952 precipitation averaged 46.60 inches (0.86 inch below normal); new minimum water levels in nine wells.
